decisions.reason: As a flagship product very close to the firm's core dosimetry and QA knowledge and still promoted on the home page across 2023-2024, it fits the firm's strongest absorptive capacity and is unlikely to be withdrawn.

This oncology risk management software builds on the firm's established clinical QA workflows and software integration capabilities, so management would expect to learn and improve it rather than exit quickly.
A CT image quality phantom is adjacent to the firm's imaging QA competences and accredited measurement culture, making it a natural extension that the firm is well placed to refine.

The mammography image quality phantom is more distant from the firm's main radiation therapy base, but it still leverages related imaging QA knowledge, so management would more likely keep it while testing market traction.

Because the full field mammography test phantom sits in a less familiar niche for the firm and has only very recent market evidence, withdrawal risk is higher, but related imaging and calibration know-how still argues for continued commercialization.

This flagship medical imaging QA instrument line aligns closely with the firm's stated direction, broad technical base, and ability to absorb and apply adjacent knowledge from R&D and research cooperation, so it is likely to be retained.
